A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained content against additions.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results, proofs and illustrative functions, but no original experimental or data-analysis outcomes. Figure 3 illustrates an analytically defined function.

after.justification: Section 6 reports two original synthetic experiments with numerical test errors in Tables 3–4 and training details in Appendix C. These establish empirical results despite the checklist's contradictory statement that the work has no experiments.

M1.justification: The MoE definition, routing mechanism and constructive expert designs are retained. v2 elaborates the existing nonlinear-router suggestion and evaluates particular model configurations without introducing a new proposed algorithm or component.

E1.justification: v2 introduces empirical coverage absent from v1: regression on a circle embedded in higher-dimensional space and approximation of a compositional function over nine regions. The latter function already appeared as an illustration, but is newly used for evaluation.

E2.justification: Experiment II adds one evaluated comparator: shallow 1-6-MoE against deep 2-3-MoE, described as having comparable parameter counts. v1's dense-network comparison is theoretical, and no empirical dense baseline is added.

E3.justification: v2 establishes new experimental protocols: ambient dimensions 16–128 with expert width 10, and expert widths 16–128 for the depth comparison. Appendix C specifies online squared-loss training with Adam, batch size 128 and budgets of 2,000 or 5,000 iterations. These are new evaluations, not revised settings for earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 introduce empirical tests of both central structural hypotheses: sensitivity to ambient dimension and the role of depth as expert width increases. v1 contains no corresponding empirical sensitivity studies or architectural comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 explicitly declines error bars in its checklist, calling approximation error deterministic, but introduces no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds all experimental results. Table 3 reports errors between 3.17e-4 and 3.42e-4 across dimensions. In Table 4, 2-3-MoE improves from 8.32e-5 to 2.59e-6 as width increases; 1-6-MoE is slightly better at width 16 but worse at width 128, with 4.60e-5. These are newly reported outcomes, not improvements over v1 measurements.

T1.justification: The principal assumptions, approximation bounds and proof constructions in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–B remain unchanged. Index and dimension notation are corrected. The added non-ReLU applicability remark supplies no new formal theorem or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about manifold approximation, compositional sparsity and exponentially many task pieces. The experiments provide additional support without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly interprets stable errors across dimensions as supporting dimensionality avoidance and the shallow model's plateau as limited expressivity. Appendix A.2 adds claimed applicability to GeLU, SiLU and Swish. Existing limitations concerning other sparsity structures and training dynamics remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds concise implementation information: one A100 GPU, Adam with learning rate 1e-3, online batches of 128, squared loss and experiment-specific iteration budgets. The checklist explicitly reports no open code or data; test sampling and router implementation remain insufficiently specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zuo et al. (2021), Liu et al. (2022) and Nguyen et al. (2024) to the nonlinear-gating discussion, and Zhang et al. (2024) for the activation-extension remark. The main related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Experimental Validation, Appendix C and a NeurIPS checklist, renumbers the conclusion, and expands the nonlinear-router explanation. Most existing prose and the main narrative order are retained, with localized notation corrections.

P2.justification: Two compact experimental tables are added. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–2 retain their content. Conference-style title formatting, figure text wrapping and page reflow change the presentation without substantially redesigning the existing displays.

improvement.justification: Tables 3–4 add useful empirical illustrations of the retained theory, supported by basic training details. The gain is limited: the synthetic tests are narrow, test evaluation and uncertainty are underspecified, and the shallow-model plateau does not isolate expressivity from optimization. The checklist's claim that there are no experiments also introduces an inconsistency.
